title.value: Interactive Machine Comprehension with Information Seeking Agents
title.justification: The title is clearly mentioned at the top of the paper.
title.quote: Interactive Machine Comprehension with Information Seeking Agents

analysis.description: This paper discusses the limitations of existing machine reading comprehension (MRC) models and proposes a new method that turns MRC datasets into interactive environments. By reframing these datasets as partially observable, the paper aims to address the limitations of static datasets and enable models to seek information through sequential decision making. The authors repurpose SQuAD and NewsQA datasets and develop a baseline agent combining MRC models and reinforcement learning algorithms to test on interactive MRC tasks.

type.justification: The paper uses an empirical methodology by repurposing existing datasets (SQuAD and NewsQA), developing an agent, and conducting experiments to test it on interactive MRC tasks.
type.quote: We repurpose SQuAD and NewsQA as an initial case study, and then show how the interactive corpora can be used to train a model that seeks relevant informa- tion through sequential decision making.

name.justification: Natural Language Processing is identified as the primary field due to the focus on machine reading comprehension and question answering tasks discussed in the paper, which are core NLP tasks.
name.quote: Existing machine reading comprehension (MRC) models do not scale effectively to real-world applications like web-level information retrieval and question answering (QA).

name.justification: Machine Reading Comprehension is a direct focus of the paper, aiming at improving this task through interactive methods.
name.quote: Existing machine reading comprehension (MRC) models do not scale effectively to real-world applications.

name.justification: Reinforcement Learning is used in the methodology to train models for sequential decision making in interactive environments.
name.quote: This casts MRC as a sequential decision-making prob- lem amenable to reinforcement learning (RL).

name.justification: The QA-DQN is identified as the baseline agent used in the experiments part of the research.
name.quote: As a baseline agent, we adopt QA-DQN (Yuan et al., 2019), we modify it to enable extractive QUERY generation and question answering.

is_contributed.justification: The QA-DQN is referenced as an existing model and adapted for use in the research, indicating it's not a novel contribution of this paper.
is_contributed.quote: As a baseline agent, we adopt QA-DQN (Yuan et al., 2019).

is_executed.justification: The QA-DQN model is used in the experiments conducted as part of the research.
is_executed.quote: We conduct experiments on several variants of iMRC and discuss the significant challenges posed by our setting.

is_compared.justification: The paper compares the performance of QA-DQN in the context of the new iMRC task they defined.
is_compared.quote: We develop a baseline agent that combines a top performing MRC model and two state-of- the-art RL optimization algorithms and test it on iMRC tasks.
